decided.question: what GET …/request-topics answers for a status outside active | archived | all
decided.chose: refuse with 400 REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.statusUnknown ('Choose a valid status'), an omitted status still meaning active
decided.rejected: falling back to the active default, which is the empty-catalogue-from-a-typo outcome TC-02-INT-04 exists to prevent
decided.why: rule 2 — the sibling parameter on the same read already refuses, and the requests list read in this same spec refuses an unrecognised status rather than defaulting it
decided.recordedAt: REQ-02-002, now 'the audience and the read's status are closed sets', which states both refusals in its rule sentence; the message's row in the Error Messages table and the GET request-topics row of the Routes table; the Query paragraph under that route; and TC-02-INT-04, which reads status=activ and asserts the 400

decided.question: whether the ordering control always reorders the list, when its computed value is clamped to 0 and 32767
decided.chose: the clamp wins: up sends the row above's sortOrder minus one and down the row below's plus one, and against a neighbour already holding 0 or 32767 the moved row clamps onto the neighbour's own value, the two tie, and the name tiebreak decides — so that one press can leave the list as it was and every other press reorders it
decided.rejected: the claim that the list always comes back reordered, which the clamp makes false; sending the neighbour's own value on every press, which ties on every move rather than only at the bound; and a second PATCH renumbering the neighbour, which makes one press into a pair of writes with no lock between them
decided.why: rule 3 — the clamp is the rule that refuses to invent a value outside the column's range, and the alternative that would keep the promise needs a second write the spec's one-PATCH-per-move rule forecloses
decided.recordedAt: the contracts' Screens section, the paragraph under the Settings mock and the Decided note beside it; the consequence is carried into Known Gaps row 5 of 02-request-topics.md, which now names the bound alongside the closed gap

decided.question: what the Request topics address draws for a member without manage-request-topics
decided.chose: no topics page at all: request-topics-page, request-topics-add-btn and every row control absent, nothing drawn in their place, and the browser sent to /org/{orgId}/members, which every role can open; the write routes answer 403 regardless
decided.rejected: a read-only catalogue, which GET …/request-topics would serve to a user under REQ-02-008 but which offers a screen whose every control is missing
decided.why: rule 1 — the settings screen this repository already ships for a caller without its capability redirects to the members list and draws nothing while it does, and rule 3, since the narrower answer withholds the screen rather than half of it
decided.recordedAt: the UI Description row 'Permission-limited (user, viewer)', where the choice and the rejected alternative are written; the request-topics-page row of the Required data-testid table; and TC-02-E2E-05, whose Expected Result now says the direct navigation lands on the members list

decided.question: whether the vacation cards on the requests list adopt Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed
decided.chose: they do not: the map covers the stored statuses of a Request and nothing else, and a vacation card goes on reading Pending, Approved, Rejected or Cancelled from its own stored value, so selecting Closed can leave a card reading Rejected beside a request reading Closed
decided.rejected: relabelling vacations through the same map, which would call an approved vacation Completed and a rejected one Closed
decided.why: rule 4 — the narrower rule, scoped to the entity this spec has requirements about; renaming a vacation decision is a change no requirement here asks for and cannot be taken back once screens read it
decided.recordedAt: the contracts' Status Labels section, the paragraph and Decided note under the table; TC-02-UNIT-05 now claims an entry for each stored Request status and none for a vacation's

decided.question: whether the staff seed stays wider than the four topics the request named
decided.chose: it stays: beside VPN, Claude, Question and Other the staff seed names the access kinds the retired accessKind dial offered — repository, environment, server, vpn, admin_panel, documentation — so an organization that classified requests by that dial finds the same words in the catalogue
decided.rejected: cutting the seed to VPN, Claude, Question and Other and letting a curator add the rest, which hands every organization the same list to re-type and makes the catalogue narrower than the vocabulary the product already had
decided.why: rule 1 — the code's own ACCESS_KINDS is the vocabulary being replaced, and the spec never took a contrary position; Known Gaps already reasons about the seed as that set, naming saas and an access Other as the two it omits
decided.recordedAt: the contracts' Seed Data section, the Decided note under the table

decided.question: what a sortOrder that is not an integer answers, when an out-of-range integer is clamped

decided.why: rule 2 — this spec's own refusal discipline for a field it cannot honour, and rule 3, the answer that refuses
